issue.title: Bug: `start.sh` in syncd startup is sometimes run twice

failure.body:
### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

High

### Description of the bug

When the Syncd docker is created it runs a few programs that are dependent on each other completing.
https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/blob/master/platform/broadcom/docker-syncd-brcm-dnx/supervisord.conf#L22-L69
```
program:rsyslogd
program:start
   dependent_startup_wait_for=rsyslogd:running
program:syncd
   dependent_startup_wait_for=start:exited
```

`rsyslogd` running triggers `start` and `start` exiting triggers `syncd`.

However, occasionally we see the `start` program triggered twice:
```
cmp214-5 INFO syncd0#supervisord 2025-10-30 <IPV6>,662 INFO spawned: 'start' with pid 20
cmp214-5 INFO syncd0#supervisord 2025-10-30 <IPV6>,745 INFO success: start entered RUNNING state, process has stayed up for > than 0 seconds (startsecs)
cmp214-5 INFO syncd0#supervisord 2025-10-30 <IPV6>,749 INFO exited: start (exit status 0; expected)
cmp214-5 INFO syncd0#supervisord 2025-10-30 <IPV6>,773 INFO spawned: 'start' with pid 28
cmp214-5 INFO syncd0#supervisord 2025-10-30 <IPV6>,774 INFO success: start entered RUNNING state, process has stayed up for > than 0 seconds (startsecs)
cmp214-5 INFO syncd0#supervisord 2025-10-30 <IPV6>,836 INFO spawned: 'syncd' with pid 35
cmp214-5 INFO syncd0#supervisord 2025-10-30 <IPV6>,915 INFO success: syncd entered RUNNING state, process has stayed up for > than 1 seconds (startsecs)
cmp214-5 INFO syncd0#supervisord 2025-10-30 <IPV6>,931 INFO exited: start (exit status 0; expected)
cmp214-5 INFO syncd0#supervisord 2025-10-30 <IPV6>,942 INFO spawned: 'ledinit' with pid 56
cmp214-5 INFO syncd0#supervisord 2025-10-30 <IPV6>,942 INFO success: ledinit entered RUNNING state, process has stayed up for > than 0 seconds (startsecs)
```

The problem here is that the `syncd` program will start running while the second `start` program is still running.
This causes issues if the `start.sh` script is executing it's `cp $HWSKU_DIR/sai.profile /etc/sai.d/sai.profile` operation at the same time the `syncd` program is reading the `sai.profile`.
https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/blob/master/platform/broadcom/docker-syncd-brcm-dnx/start.sh#L29C9-L29C57
https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-sairedis/blob/master/syncd/Syncd.cpp#L3917-L3960

If this occurs `syncd` will read an empty file and then no `SAI_INIT_CONFIG_FILE` is passed to the SAI/SDK.
```
> cat /etc/sai.d/sai.profile
SAI_INIT_CONFIG_FILE=/usr/share/sonic/hwsku/j2p-a7800r3a-36d-36x400G.config.bcm
SAI_SWITCH_NON_ECMP_MAX_SIZE=3072
```

### Steps to Reproduce

To reproduce this we found it easiest to trigger `config reloads` many times back to back.
We wrote a sonic-mgmt test to do this:
```
from tests.common.helpers.multi_thread_utils import SafeThreadPoolExecutor
from tests.common.config_reload import config_reload
import time

def run_config_reload(duthosts):
    with SafeThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=8) as executor:
        for duthost in duthosts:
            # Safe reload to make sure critical processes is up
            executor.submit(
                config_reload,
                duthost, config_source='config_db', safe_reload=True, check_intf_up_ports=True,
            )
    time.sleep(60)  # Wait for a bit before starting next test when running consecutively

def test_config_reload(duthosts):
    for i in range(30):
        print("Iteration " + str(i))
        run_config_reload(duthosts)
```

I found I'd hit this problem a few times in a run

### Actual Behavior and Expected Behavior

The `start` program in Syncd startup should only be run a single time, currently it's seen to run twice occasionally.

resolution.title: [Arista][DNX] Workaround for sai.profile being empty when syncd starts
resolution.description:
Original PR https://github.com/Azure/sonic-buildimage-msft/pull/1770 went only to msft-202405 but the issue with `start.sh` running twice hasn't been fixed https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/issues/24399 so creating a PR for master and hopefully cast to 202511.

We're seeing an issue where start.sh is run multiple times on syncd startup and if the 'cp' operation in the 2nd start.sh occurs while the Syncd process is reading the /etc/sai.d/sai.profile it will end up reading an empty file.

Therefor if we skip the 'cp' operation when the file is unchanged the 2nd start.sh run should always be a no-op.

This is a workaround until we find the reason and solution to stop start.sh from running multiple times.
